claims.text: Rapidly quenched phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys typically have marginal glass-forming ability.
Rapidly quenched phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys typically have moderate amorphous thermal stability.
A small microalloying addition improves glass-forming ability relative to the alloy without the addition.
A small microalloying addition improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to the alloy without the addition.
The microalloying addition increases local atomic packing disorder.
The microalloying addition increases local chemical heterogeneity.
Increased local atomic packing disorder and chemical heterogeneity hinder crystalline nucleation.
The microalloying addition disrupts regular atomic arrangements.
The microalloying addition reduces atomic mobility during cooling.
Disruption of regular atomic arrangements and reduced atomic mobility retard crystalline-phase nucleation.
Retarded crystalline-phase nucleation stabilizes the amorphous structure.
The modified alloy will have a lower critical cooling rate for glass formation than the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will have a higher crystallization onset temperature than the unmodified baseline.
The beneficial effect occurs only within a narrow range of microalloying concentrations.
Rapid quenching is required for the beneficial effect.
Microalloying concentrations outside the beneficial window may produce no improvement or may deteriorate glass-forming characteristics.
